clue.text: Superb line inserted in part of speech

indicators.note: inserted in tells us the line abbreviation goes inside the grammatical term

parts.note: a part of speech such as noun or verb is a word class

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson praising a superb line slipped into a passage of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inserted in' puts L inside WORD CLASS, the grammarians' name for a part of speech, splitting WORD after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something world-class is among the best anywhere, which is what superb conveys.

clue.text: Least significant part of Christian festival

definitions.meaning: the tiniest bit, as in 'not a jot or tittle'
..., short for Whitsun or Pentecost, seven weeks after Easter

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the smallest piece of a church holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two definitions: one sense is a tiny amount, the other the feast also called Whitsun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny scrap is a jot, and Pentecost is commonly called Whitsun in Britain, shortened in compounds like Whit Monday.

clue.text: Travelled across bay, say?

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse, so travelling astride one is going on horseback rather than over water

explanation.surface: A journey over a stretch of coastal water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like an inlet of the sea, but it is a horse of that colour; 'say' marks it as just one example of a mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on horseback is the past tense of the verb to ride, so travelling on a bay horse fits.

clue.text: Verdi's unusual tempo, new to light music

indicators.note: unusual means the composer's name is set out in a different order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the name itself is the fodder
in music the tempo is the time a piece is taken at
taken as written

explanation.surface: Verdi taking an odd speed in a piece of light music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges VERDI to DIVER; 'tempo' looks like anagram fodder but is a synonym, TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light, entertaining instrumental suite, as Mozart wrote for social occasions.

clue.text: Lady, I? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be put in another order

parts.note: the word lady plus the letter I supply the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman wondering whether she herself might be the person meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging LADY and I gives a woman's name, and a lady saying 'I' might well be called that.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, so a lady referring to herself might be one.

clue.text: Elegant eccentric used to carry out financial transactions

definitions.text: used to carry out financial transactions

parts.note: smart means stylish or elegant
a card is an informal word for an eccentric, amusing person

explanation.surface: A stylish oddball handling money deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' reads as an adjective but is a noun: a character, or CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip-bearing plastic card is used for payments and banking, which is what the definition describes.

clue.text: Detailed description of fungi brought back from East

indicators.note: brought back from East means read from the right-hand end, so the word is reversed

parts.note: ceps are edible mushrooms, porcini

explanation.surface: A thorough account of mushrooms imported from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back from East' looks like importing from Asia but means writing CEPS from the right, giving SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specification, an exact listing of requirements or features.

clue.text: Confined a medicine in a sort of scale

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: A drug kept in a weighing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' suggests weighing apparatus, but it is the musical kind; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-note musical scale is called pentatonic, so the answer names a type of scale.

clue.text: European said to indicate where travellers are inspected

indicators.note: said means the word for the European is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic
to point is to indicate or show

explanation.surface: A European reportedly showing where border officials examine visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the Czech, which sounds like CHECK; POINT is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or security post where passports and vehicles are examined is a checkpoint.

clue.text: One person's home split in two parts

parts.note: in means at home
to divi (or divvy) is to split or share out
dual means made of two parts

explanation.surface: A single householder's house divided into a pair of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' after 'split' is only a link word. Divi, or divvy, is British slang for sharing something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Individual means belonging to a single person, as in individual portions.

clue.text: Formerly suspended after one's ejected from centre

indicators.note: ejected from centre means a letter is removed from the middle of the word

parts.note: on ice means put on hold, suspended
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a time a player was suspended after being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link; ON ICE loses its central I.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, which is what formerly means.

clue.text: Produce splendid show in base, equipped with visual aid

indicators.note: in tells us the show goes inside the base

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a bed of concrete
to make a spectacle is to produce a splendid show

explanation.surface: Putting on a grand display at headquarters, with the help of a viewing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container indicator. 'Produce splendid show' reads like a verb phrase, but it gives one noun, as in 'make a spectacle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing glasses is bespectacled; spectacles are an aid to sight.

clue.text: Win an excessive amount, as bore might, with disastrous results

definitions.meaning: the gambler's idiom for winning more than the casino can pay

definitions.text: as bore might, with disastrous results
definitions.meaning: a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river, which might burst over its banks

explanation.surface: A gambler winning big, compared to a boring person causing havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' tempts as a tedious person, but it is a tidal surge on a river such as the Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking the bank at a casino means winning more than it holds; a river bore can literally breach banks.

clue.text: Give weapons to a scoundrel in hat — that could cover one's tracks

indicators.note: in places the arming and the scoundrel inside the hat

parts.note: a tam is a tam-o'-shanter, a Scottish cap
to arm is to give weapons
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Arming a villain wearing a hat, who can then conceal his trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover one's tracks' sounds like hiding evidence, but it means surfacing roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmacadam is the road surface of tar and stones, used to pave roads and paths.

clue.text: Dreadful exposure almost did in this tragic hero

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Being shamefully exposed nearly destroyed a hero of Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DID to DI; EXPOSURE plus DI is then rearranged under 'Dreadful'. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' tragedy is named after its hero, the king of Thebes who killed his father and married his mother.

clue.text: Part of steamer I can acquire for continental collection

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller buying a piece of a steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for' into the definition; it is the link word, since 'for continental collection' cannot stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are objects typical of America, so it is a collection from that continent.

clue.text: Whatever happens, regardless of the speed

definitions.meaning: in any case, come what may

explanation.surface: Someone insisting on going ahead however fast things move.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally, with rate meaning speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in any event, and literally means at whatever speed.

clue.text: Band put on concert as publicity event

indicators.note: put on means the band comes after the concert in this across entry

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, like the BBC Proms
a band or ring is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A group performs at a gig to get some publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians, but it is a ring, the shape O. The Proms are London's summer concert season.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is short for a promotion, an event or clip that advertises something.

clue.text: State in East, on ocean

indicators.note: on means the compass letter is added after the ocean in an across entry

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A place in the east, by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: The origin of dependence, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: The origin of dependence, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in puts the initial letter inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking or enunciating

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone musing on where dependence starts, loosely speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an addiction is, so to speak, where dependence comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependence on a substance or habit.

clue.text: Consider transformation of Mary now she's rustic

parts.note: to count someone something is to consider them so

indicators.note: transformation means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reflecting on how Mary has changed into a country girl.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNT is followed by RYWOMAN, from rearranging MARY NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman living in rural parts is a countrywoman, so a rustic woman fits.

clue.text: Oxford scholar upset company on varsity's river

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits on top of the second in this down entry
upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river at Cambridge, the university town

explanation.surface: An Oxford academic upset that a firm is operating on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Varsity is British slang for university, especially Oxford or Cambridge. William of Occam was a medieval Oxford philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Occam, of Occam's razor, was a 14th-century Oxford-educated Franciscan philosopher.

clue.text: Product of the numbers before and the one after

definitions.text: Product of the numbers before and the one after

parts.words: Product of the numbers before and the one after
parts.note: this clue is number 22: multiply the digit 2 before by the 2 after

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle about consecutive numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: it sits at 22, so the 2 before times the 2 after. The '.'' in the held text is an OCR smudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times two gives this number, the product of the clue number's digits.

clue.text: Raised guns and hunted animal

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: gats is old slang for guns

explanation.surface: Lifting shotguns at a quarry pursued by the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised guns' looks like aiming, but GATS is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, traditionally hunted with hounds.

clue.text: Fish from front or stern of dinghy

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
the stern of a boat is its back, so the word's last letter

explanation.surface: A fish caught from the bow or stern of a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' and 'stern' both apply to dinghy: its first letter, OR as written, then its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dory is a sea fish, the John Dory, also a name for a small flat-bottomed boat.

clue.text: How something's sent from place, with ports involved?

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Asking how goods are shipped out from a town with harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'with' are link words; the letters of PLACE and PORTS together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcel post is the postal service for sending packages, a way of dispatching items.

clue.text: Almost saw what garment is not revealing?

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a maxim

explanation.surface: Someone almost glimpsed a garment that shows very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see, but it is a proverb, MAXIM, which loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long skirt or dress reaching the ankles, so it reveals little leg.

clue.text: Arrangement for yacht when Queen Maud's at sea in sailing ship

indicators.note: in puts the queen and the jumbled name inside the ship

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the name's letters are mixed up

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the name is the fodder

explanation.surface: The Queen and Maud are aboard a sailing ship, discussing how a yacht is set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges MAUD to give MUDA, and 'in' puts the queen with it inside the ship. A Bermuda rig is named after the island where the design began.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bermuda rig is a triangular-sail arrangement used on most modern yachts.
